The Sea of Galilee, or the plain on its north-west shore, Israel.

A town in the hills above the north shore of the Sea of Galilee; ruins at Korazim, Israel.
The village of the wedding feast; in Galilee, Israel, at Kafr Kanna near Nazareth or at Khirbet Qana.
The village where Jesus raised a widow's son; Nein, below Mount Tabor, Israel.

People of Gadara, a Greek town south-east of the Sea of Galilee; Umm Qais, Jordan.
The river that runs from the Sea of Galilee down to the Dead Sea; today the border of Israel and the West Bank with the country of Jordan.

A great Phoenician port; Saida, Lebanon.
The town where Elijah stayed with a widow; Sarafand, between Tyre and Sidon, Lebanon.
The Lebanon mountains, famous for their cedars; Lebanon.

The town where Peter healed Aeneas; Lod, Israel.

One of the five Philistine cities; Gaza.

One of the five Philistine cities; Tel Miqne, Israel.

The land of the Philistines on the southern coast; Gaza and south-west Israel.
Acre, a port on the north coast; Akko, Israel.
The hill country east of the Jordan; northern Jordan.
The fertile plateau east of the Sea of Galilee; the Golan Heights and southern Syria.
The land east of the Dead Sea, Ruth's homeland; Jordan.
The land of the Ammonites around their capital Rabbah; Amman, Jordan.
Capital of the Ammonites; Amman, Jordan.

The mountains of Edom; southern Jordan.
Capital of Sihon, king of the Amorites; Tell Hesban, Jordan.
A city of Moab; Dhiban, Jordan.
The mountain from which Moses saw the Promised Land before he died; Mount Nebo, near Madaba, Jordan.
The ridge of which Mount Nebo is a peak; near Madaba, Jordan.

The river where Jacob wrestled with the angel; the Zarqa River, Jordan.

Jabesh-gilead, a town in Gilead that Saul saved; northern Jordan.
Where Jacob saw God face to face, by the Jabbok; northern Jordan.

The mountain where God gave the Law; by tradition Jebel Musa in the south of the Sinai Peninsula, Egypt.

The land Jacob's family lived in, in the east of the Nile Delta, Egypt. (In Joshua also a district of southern Judah.)
A store city built by the Israelites; Pi-Ramesses, at Qantir in the Nile Delta, Egypt.
The land of Jethro, where Moses lived as a shepherd; north-west Saudi Arabia, east of the Gulf of Aqaba.
The desert lands east and south of Israel; today Jordan and Saudi Arabia.
A land famous for its gold; its site is not known (south Arabia, East Africa and India have been proposed).
A far-off port in the west; probably Tartessos in southern Spain.

The old capital of Egypt; Mit Rahina, south of Cairo.
Zoan, a capital in the Nile Delta; San el-Hagar, Egypt.

Upper Egypt, the Nile valley south of Cairo.
The great port founded by Alexander the Great; Alexandria, Egypt.

The land around Babylon; southern Iraq.
The land of the Chaldeans, who ruled Babylon in the time of the Exile; southern Iraq.
Abraham's first home; Tell el-Muqayyar, southern Iraq.
Where Abraham lived before going to Canaan, and where Jacob found Rachel; Harran, south-east Turkey.
The land between the Euphrates and the Tigris; Iraq, north-east Syria and south-east Turkey.

The river flowing through Turkey and Iraq, past Nineveh and Baghdad.
The empire that destroyed the northern kingdom of Israel; northern Iraq.

Where Babylon defeated Egypt in 605 BC; Karkamış, on the Turkey-Syria border.
A city on the Orontes; Hama, Syria. "The entrance of Hamath" marks Israel's northern border.
An old city, capital of Aram; Damascus, capital of Syria. Paul was converted on the road to it.
The empire of Cyrus, who let the Jews go home; Iran.
The land of the Medes; north-west Iran, around Hamadan.
A city of Media in the Book of Tobit; Rey, south of Tehran, Iran.
Capital of the Persian kings, the setting of Esther; Shush, Iran.
A region of Edom; southern Jordan.
An oasis town in Arabia; Tayma, Saudi Arabia.
A trading people and oasis in Arabia; al-Ula, Saudi Arabia.
Job's land; probably in Edom or east of the Jordan, southern Jordan.

The region around Tarsus; south-east Turkey.

The southern coast around Antalya, Turkey.
Inland hill country of south-west Turkey.

A town of Lycaonia; near Karaman, Turkey.

North-west Turkey, on the Black Sea.
North-east Turkey, on the Black Sea.

A port on the south-west coast of Turkey, near Gelemiş.
A Greek island, where Titus led the Church.
The Roman province of northern Greece.

The Roman province of southern Greece, with its capital at Corinth.
The Roman province on the east coast of the Adriatic; today Croatia, Bosnia, Montenegro and Albania.
The port where Paul landed in Italy; Pozzuoli, near Naples.
